newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY FLOATS UP VS BASKET, DEPOS STAY ABOVE 20 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY FLOATS UP VS BASKET, DEPOS STAY ABOVE 20 PCT.

text.p: The Polish zloty floated just up against the currency basket in very light turnover anchored by a nearly flat dollar/mark in European trade, dealers said.

They said some small-scale dollar selling orders, most likely coming from corporate clients, lifted the zloty, but that banks were not in a speculative mood on Monday and trade remained thin throughout the day.

"It was quite calm today as the dollar/mark barely budged all day," said Marcin Trzykowski of Pekao SA. "Some players sold currencies, likely for clients, but no strong trends developed as amounts were small," he added.
The zloty closed at 1.96/1.90 percent from the parity rate, up from Friday's 1.85/1.80 percent.
It was at 2.8125/30 to the dollar, up from 2.8145/55 on Friday and at 1.8375/90 to the mark, up from 1.8379/89.

One-day deposits remained above 20 percent despite Monday's 74 million zloty net inflow into the system and dealers said call money rates would likely remain above the main 14-day drainage rate of 19.14 percent for the rest of the week.
"Wednesday's large cash inflow will be offset by T-bill payments and rates are not likely to fall to reverse-repo levels soon," one foreign bank dealer said.
Overnight rates closed at 20.0/20.5 percent against Friday's 20.2/20.5 percent, and tomorrow/next deposits were at 20.45/20.55 percent, versus last week's 20.20/20.55.

The treasury sold 740 million zlotys worth of T-bills at today's primary tender and average yields for the 52-week, 26-week and 13-week paper held flat at 19.43, 19.09 and 18.55 percent. The 8-week paper yield fell 0.07 to 18.11 percent.

The central bank said Poland had a current account surplus of $58 million in August, bringing the January-August surplus to $48 million. It said official reserves grew $187 million to $17.97 billion in August. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
